diagnostic_evidence.quote: The HJB inequality \eqref{eq:hjb} (or its LMI equivalent \eqref{eq:lmi});

issues.failure_explanation: The SDP imposes the LMI only at the collocation points x_j. The suboptimality and stability theorems require the HJB inequality or a residual bound for every x in Ω. The source gives no argument or residual bound showing that satisfaction at the collocation points implies satisfaction on all of Ω, and the convergence theorem only concerns approximation of V*, not the residual of the SDP solution. Thus the computed SDP solution need not satisfy the hypotheses of the performance guarantees.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a residual or collocation-error theorem that bounds R(x) on Ω in terms of collocation residuals and fill distance, or enforce/validate the inequality on all of Ω.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised suboptimality, stability, and convergence guarantees are not established for the finite-dimensional SDP actually solved.
issues.title: Collocation SDP enforces the LMI only at finite points, not on all of Ω
issues.why_classification: Without such a bridge, the algorithmic guarantee changes from a continuous HJB certificate to only finite-point constraints; a new nontrivial approximation/validation argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: so $\hat{V}(x) \geq V^*(x) - \epsilon \cdot T(x)$ follows from standard perturbation arguments.

issues.failure_explanation: The residual assumption is one-sided, R≥-ε. Under the feedback, this gives dV/dt + cost ≥ -ε, which integrates to J ≥ V(x0)-V(xT)-εT, not J ≤ V(x0)-V(xT)+εT. Thus the proof derives the opposite inequality. The lower bound 0≤V-V* is not implied and is false in general; for example, with a stable linear system one can take V=V*-δφ with φ vanishing on the boundary and small δ so that R≥-ε while V<V* inside. The upper bound V-V*≤εT is also not established by the given argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a two-sided residual bound, e.g. |R|≤ε, and redo the comparison with V*, or replace the lower bound by the correct one-sided estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The suboptimality bound and the control suboptimality corollary are unreliable; the claimed optimality guarantee is not established.
issues.title: Suboptimality theorem has a false lower bound and sign-reversed proof
issues.why_classification: The central suboptimality guarantee is false as stated and the proof's sign error cannot be fixed by a local edit without changing the residual hypotheses or conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof actually yields a rate depending on c3, which is tied to the state cost q, not on λ_min(P). For the scalar system A=0, B=1, D=1, q(x)=0.005x^2 (Q=0.01), the ARE gives P=0.1 and the closed-loop rate is 0.1, while λ_min(P)/λ_max(P)=1. Thus the stated lower bound on β is false.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $V^* \in H^s(\Omega)$ (Sobolev space of order $s$) with $s > n/2$.
The Gaussian kernel generates an RKHS $\mathcal{H}_\kappa$ that is norm-equivalent to certain Sobolev spaces.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem only assumes V*∈H^s(Ω), but the proof's approximation step requires V*∈H_κ. The Gaussian kernel's RKHS is not norm-equivalent to a Sobolev space; it is a much smaller space of analytic functions. Thus the proof does not establish the stated rate for arbitrary V*∈H^s, and the norm-equivalence claim is false.

Its Hessian at the origin is Q=0, not the chosen Q=2. Also ∇²V*(0)=2, while the imposed Riccati value is P=1+√3≈2.732. The example is therefore inconsistent with the standing assumptions and with the Riccati Hessian constraint.
